title: Telemetry Wrangler: tenant-aware capture flags, field-level consent tagging, and audit trails
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Goal: provide an operational playbook and implementation for tenant-aware trace capture flags, granular consent tagging on telemetry fields, and an immutable access/audit trail for observability queries. This ticket covers: (1) tracing hook changes to attach capture/consent metadata from request context without leaking PII into indexed traces, (2) pipeline transforms for logs/metrics that perform field-level redaction with policy-driven TTLs, and (3) RBAC + access logging for any human or service reads of raw telemetry. Expected outcomes: safer multi-tenant observability data, configurable retention backed by enforcement, and dashboards that surface latency/error by tenant without exposing redacted fields.
acceptance_criteria: Tracing hooks add capture_flag and consent_tags to spans as non-indexed attributes and do not persist raw user-provided PII into trace index
Pipeline transform supports declarative redaction rules (field regex/semantic labels) with tenant-specific TTLs and a dry-run mode
Access to raw (pre-redaction) telemetry requires explicit RBAC permission and generates an immutable audit log entry (user, reason, query, time)
Dashboards show per-tenant latency/error trends after transformations and include a metric for percentage of traces redacted
End-to-end latency impact of instrumentation on p99 trace ingestion remains < 6% at target QPS compared to baseline
Documentation and runbook published with step-by-step rollback and emergency reveal procedures
implementation_notes: Will add a small tracing shim in the agents that copies capture_flag and consent_tags from request headers/context into span attributes, marked as non-indexable to avoid accidental search
Pipeline will use an intermediate 'sanitization' stage in the logs/metrics ingestion cluster; rules stored in a central policy service (policy defs are JSON, evaluated in Rust for speed)
Retention enforcement implemented as metadata on the sanitization output: encrypted TTL token + tenant id; background pruner deletes per policy
Access ledger is append-only in our existing observability metadata store; reads require a scoped token exchange validated by the control plane
We will ship dry-run across 10% of traffic in Canary A, then 50%, monitor regressions and error budgets before full rollout
Fallback plan: disable sanitization stage to restore raw telemetry to debugging-only buckets while preserving audit trail
perf_measurements: Benchmark strategy: simulate 2k QPS with mixed trace sizes (avg 12 spans, 4KB payload) and compare ingestion latency and CPU between baseline and sanitization-on
Target: additional CPU < 10% for sanitization stage, p99 ingestion latency delta < 6%
Measure disk and S3 egress increase due to redaction metadata and access-ledger entries
Create automated perf job linked to PR to prevent regressions

2025-02-18 | Priya Narang (Security): Reviewed approach. Strong request to avoid storing any raw PII in index; prefer deterministic tokenization for fields marked 'revealable' only. Security review scheduled.
